desc:
The Hamming distance between two integers is the number of bit positions at which they differ.

Given the array nums, return the sum of the Hamming distances over all pairs of indices i < j. Equal values at different indices form separate pairs.

nums = [4, 14, 2] -> 6   (distances 2, 2 and 2)
nums = [4, 14, 4] -> 4   (distances 2, 0 and 2)
hints: Comparing every pair of numbers bit by bit is too slow when there are thousands of numbers. Can you count per bit position instead?
For a fixed bit position, suppose c numbers have that bit set. Then exactly c * (n - c) pairs differ at that position.
Add c * (n - c) over all 31 bit positions. Each position takes one pass over the array.
editorial: The total is the sum over pairs of the number of differing bit positions. Swap the order of the two sums: for each bit position, count the pairs whose two numbers disagree there. Pairs disagree at a position exactly when one number has the bit and the other does not, so with c ones and n - c zeros there are c * (n - c) such pairs.
Every value fits in 31 bits, so there are 31 positions and the work is O(31 n), which is linear. The answer is at most about 1.25 * 108 with the given limits, so it fits in 32 bits.
